question: Who will fly to ISS under Axiom-4 mission in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shubhanshu Shukla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shubhanshu Shukla** has been selected to fly to the International Space Station (ISS) as part of the **Axiom-4 mission**, scheduled for June 2025.
 
• The Axiom-4 mission is a collaboration between **Axiom Space** and NASA, aiming to expand private missions to the ISS.
 
• Shubhanshu Shukla, an Indian-origin astronaut, will represent a significant milestone in India's growing participation in international space exploration.
 
• This mission will include scientific research and technology demonstrations aimed at advancing human space exploration capabilities.
 
• Axiom Space has previously conducted successful private crewed missions to the ISS, paving the way for commercial space travel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Space Station (ISS):**

 
 
• The ISS is a modular space station orbiting Earth, serving as a research laboratory in low Earth orbit.
 
• It involves international collaboration from NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA, and CSA.
 
• The station facilitates research in microgravity and space environments to develop technologies for long-term human exploration.
 
 
 
• **Axiom Space:**
 
 
• Axiom Space is a private space company based in the United States, focused on building the first commercial space station.
 
• It conducts private crewed missions to the ISS and is developing modules for future commercial use.
 
 
 
• **Private Space Missions:**
 
 
• Private missions allow commercial entities to access space for research, tourism, and technology development.
 
• They represent a growing trend in the space industry, supported by collaborations with agencies like NASA.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Goals of Axiom Missions:**
 
 
• These missions aim to conduct cutting-edge research in areas like biotechnology, materials science, and space sustainability.
 
• They also support the development of commercial space infrastructure and technologies.
